source: Failure as a Process: An Anatomy of CLI Coding Agent Trajectories
summary: July 2026 study of 1,794 CLI coding-agent trajectories across 7 frontier models. Finds failures are epistemic, start within first few steps, agents continue spending compute after recovery is impossible. 71% of successes contained at least one recovered error.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly supports partial retry (HID-186) and automatic retry (HID-167); failure taxonomy could inform retry classification. Theme fully covered by existing open issues.

source: PAUSE: Search-Free Steering of Coding Agents Before Their First Source-Code Edit
summary: October 2026 paper proposing a mid-run Planner intervention exactly at the first source-code edit. Reports +16.8% on SWE-bench Verified with Qwen3-coder + GPT-5.6-Sol. Offline variant restores an earlier reasoning checkpoint and appends a new plan.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — could inform a mid-implementation plan-refresh step between Implementation and AIReview. HID-93 (adversarial plan critique) partially overlaps; backlog at 11 open issues blocks creation.

source: Strained Coherence: A Pre-Failure Signal in Coding Agent Execution Trajectories
summary: June 2026 paper identifying a coherence-degradation signal that precedes coding-agent failures. Proposes monitoring coherence as an early-warning mechanism before unrecoverable states.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — a coherence signal could complement automatic retry (HID-167) by triggering earlier intervention. Backlog full; HID-167 theme already open.

source: TrajAudit: Automated Failure Diagnosis for Agentic Coding Systems
summary: May 2026 paper proposing automated failure diagnosis for coding agents, categorizing failure types and recovery potential across trajectories.
relevanceToAgentForge: High theme overlap with HID-186 (partial retry) and HID-167 (automatic retry with failure classification). No new capability gap versus existing open issues.

summary: February 2026 survey organizing LLM-agent memory along substrate, cognitive mechanism (episodic, semantic, sensory, working, procedural), and memory subject (agent-centric vs user-centric). Identifies cross-session persistence as a key open problem.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — HID-188 already tracks run-outcome episodic memory injection into planner/executor. Skill distillation (distillationAgent.ts) partially addresses semantic memory. No new gap.

source: EvoMemBench: Benchmarking Agent Memory from a Self-Evolving Perspective
summary: June 2026 benchmark separating in-episode from cross-episode memory evaluation and knowledge-oriented from execution-oriented memory. Provides structured evaluation framework for agent memory systems.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — could inform acceptance criteria for HID-188 (episodic memory across runs). No new feature gap identified; existing issue covers the theme.

summary: March 2026 Karpathy project where an agent iteratively edits a training script, runs ~700 experiments over 2 days on a single GPU, and finds 20 real optimizations. Framed as a seed for self-improving research agent communities.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — RL-style self-improvement loop is explicitly a red-flag disqualifier per AgentForge research guidelines. No applicable gap in current architecture.

source: LangGraph 1.2.24 / @langchain/core 1.4.0 and Deep Agents async subagents (October-November 2026)
summary: LangGraph 1.2.24 current as of late November 2026. @langchain/core 1.4.0 adds decision models and decision-driven middleware. Deep Agents adds async (non-blocking) subagents requiring LangSmith deployment.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI subprocess model (ProcessRunner/ClaudeCodeRunner), not LangGraph. Async subagents require LangSmith infrastructure. No applicable pattern for current architecture.

summary: Industry reports note that ~50% of supervisory rules in multi-agent runs live only in natural-language prompts. Gartner predicts 40%+ of agentic AI projects canceled by 2027 due to governance gaps. Tether v0.4.0 added run-replay harness for checking tool calls and cost limits.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge already has explicit state machine (stateMachine.ts) and policy engine (policyEngine.ts) providing deterministic governance. No new gap identified.
